rationale: M60.R8 (#931) — php was the only OO lane with NO framework fixture, and the reason is visible in the artifacts: its markers were proven by script/m60/framework-surface-probe.ts, whose two php claim cases have said 'measured GAP' since 2026-09-22 and whose register records claimMisses: 2, while R8 reads MET for this lane off a runtime half (425 files, 0 findings) that cannot see a marker which never fires. Both dead markers compared against text no call site can pass: `text === "App\\"` is an exact match on a namespace string ENDING in a backslash, which no node's text carries, and `text === "TestCase"` is compared against the NAMESPACE (empty in the global namespace, and `App\Http\Controllers` here) while the base clause that names the relation is never passed to detectFramework at all. This fixture pins the two repaired spellings AND the explicit ones (`use Illuminate\...`, `use PHPUnit\Framework\...` via the base) so a repair that silences a working path fails here. It also pins the PRIMARY pick, and pins it as php's actual contract — `frameworks[0]`, i.e. DOCUMENT order. That is deliberately NOT presented as the family rule: python orders by its marker table and csharp by CS_FRAMEWORK_ORDER, so php's lack of an order table is recorded in the lane plan as a family-consistency item, and a fixture that silently blessed document order would be the defect it is meant to catch. The forbidFrameworks list is the negative half: five registered frameworks that no line of this file mentions must never appear.

expectRelationships.comment: the base clause that names the relation is also the node the PHPUnit marker must read (#931)

expectImports.comment: the explicit Laravel spelling that already worked — the prefix repair must not disturb it. php emits NO `imports` relationship (its eight labels are uses/calls/contains/references/instantiates/overrides/extends/implements), so an import is pinned through `expectImports`, not through expectRelationships

forbidRelationships.comment: no self-edge for a class with no base clause
